**The strongest direction is making checkpoint capture and sync dependable across agents, worktrees, and Entire-hosted repositories. Your Git metadata work already fits that direction.**

I reviewed the **100 latest PRs, opened September 2–9**, read the main PR descriptions, and checked open issues for potential contributions. This is an inference from public activity, rather than a confirmed internal roadmap.

| Area | What the team is working toward | Recent evidence |
|---|---|---|
| **Session ownership and checkpoint correctness** | Identify the session actually running a command, prevent one agent from adopting another’s session, and preserve accurate checkpoint data. | Stefan’s caller resolution **merged** [#2322](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2322); adoption guard [#2332](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2332) and subagent accounting [#2334](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2334) are open. Your [#2330](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2330) addresses the same reliability theme. |
| **Entire-native repositories and checkpoint storage** | Make Entire remotes the natural checkpoint destination, migrate existing history, and support native repositories consistently. | Toby’s migration command [#2327](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2327) is open; native-repo trail support [#2245](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2245) and async-only mirror creation [#2267](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2267) **merged**. |
| **Security hardening** | Ensure repository content cannot redirect file access, execute untrusted providers, bypass redaction, or choose inappropriate checkpoint sources. | Paulo’s executable resolution [#2268](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2268), filesystem boundaries [#2315](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2315), and redaction/settings/fetch protections [#2321](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2321) all **merged**. |
| **Agent compatibility and hook reliability** | Handle actual agent event formats, preserve transcripts, and make failures visible. | Open PRs cover OpenCode discovery [#2299](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2299), Claude subagent correlation [#2297](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2297), hook timeouts [#2302](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2302), and Windows prompts [#2333](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2333). |
| **Graph installation and runner usability** | Reduce setup friction for capabilities exposed through the CLI. | Ashtom’s **draft** installs Graph on demand with progress [#2324](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2324). Runner tailoring as the default [#2272](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2272) and explicit agent selection [#2306](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2306) **merged**. |

**What I’d suggest you pick up:**

1. **Best bounded task: make `entire status` report missing Git hooks — [issue #2264](https://github.com/entireio/cli/issues/2264).**  
   Today it can promise checkpoint sync while `doctor` says the hooks are absent. The issue proposes reusing the existing hook-state check. This fits the current diagnostics and hook-reliability work, has a concrete reproduction, and should be relatively contained. I found no PR explicitly referencing this issue.

2. **Best fit for your Git expertise: preserve another tool’s updated hook during reinstall — [issue #2237](https://github.com/entireio/cli/issues/2237).**  
   Entire can overwrite a newer foreign hook and continue chaining to an outdated backup. This connects directly to your Git boundary work and the ongoing Lefthook integration work. I found no PR explicitly referencing it. Build on the recently merged hook hardening in #2315.

3. **Closest to your Graph work: help finish the CLI’s on-demand Graph integration — [PR #2324](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2324).**  
   The current changes cover installation, progress, confirmation streams, and cancellation. A useful contribution would be reviewing the CLI–plugin contract and identifying any remaining failure or recovery cases. Coordinate with Ashtom because implementation is already underway.

4. **Larger product-facing follow-up: offer checkpoint migration during `repo mirror use`.**  
   Toby explicitly leaves this integration for a follow-up in [#2327](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2327): after selecting an Entire mirror, offer to move existing checkpoints there. This is a concrete extension of the storage direction, dependent on that PR settling.

Several tempting issues already have fixes underway: settings-scope leakage has [#2192](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2192), push-queue update loss has [#2012](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2012), and OpenCode session discovery has [#2299](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2299).

**My recommendation: pick #2264 for a focused next contribution, or #2237 to deepen the Git reliability work you already own.**

**I reran all three reproductions successfully on revision `5001408`.** Let’s unpack what they mean, starting with what cleanup is trying to protect.

Entire has two separate pieces:

- **Session state:** a JSON record describing a session—its phase, pending steps, base commit, and whether its work has been condensed.
- **Shadow branch:** a Git reference that keeps temporary checkpoint history reachable.

**Condensation** copies pending session data into durable checkpoint storage. Until that succeeds, deleting the shadow branch can remove the only reference keeping that history reachable.

Think of session state as a register saying **“session B still needs this storage.”** Deleting or failing to read the register does not establish that the storage is unused.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A[Session state says history is needed] --> B[Cleanup preserves shadow branch]
    B --> C[Shadow checkpoint remains reachable]
    D[State disappears from inventory] --> E[Cleanup assumes branch is unused]
    E --> F[Branch deleted]
    F --> G[Shadow-only commit becomes unreachable]
```

**1. Old session state expires even though its work is uncondensed**

Imagine an agent produces checkpoint history, then you leave the repository untouched for eight days.

Our fixture explicitly has:

```text
StepCount:       1
FullyCondensed:  false
```

The reproduction runs the same cleanup twice:

| Input | Expected | Actual |
|---|---|---|
| Last interaction one hour ago | Preserve pending history | Preserved |
| Last interaction eight days ago | Preserve pending history | State and shadow branch deleted |

The causal chain is:

```text
Cleanup lists session states
  → Load checks IsStale()
  → age exceeds seven days
  → Load deletes the state and returns “not found”
  → cleanup sees no session protecting the branch
  → deletes the branch
```

**The mistake is using age as evidence that data is disposable.** The expiry predicate does not check whether condensation succeeded.

Fresh execution output:

```text
phase=active control_deleted=0 aged_deleted=1 state_deleted=true
phase=ended  control_deleted=0 aged_deleted=1 state_deleted=true
```

Both cases left the shadow-only commit unreachable. This is distinct from #2350: every state file is valid.

**2. Cleaning one session deletes another session’s shared history**

Two sessions can share a shadow branch because its name derives from the base commit and worktree, rather than from a unique session ID.

Our setup is:

```text
Session A ─┐
           ├── shared shadow branch
Session B ─┘
```

We ask `ResetSession` to clear **A**. The expected behavior is to preserve the branch while **B** still needs it.

| B’s state | Actual result after resetting A |
|---|---|
| Valid JSON, one pending step | Shared branch survives |
| Malformed JSON | Shared branch deleted; B’s malformed file remains |

We introduce the malformed state with:

```json
{"session_id":
```

The listing silently skips B’s load error. The cleanup helper then sees nobody else using the branch.

Fresh output:

```text
corrupt=false shared_branch_exists=true  sibling_state_exists=true
corrupt=true  shared_branch_exists=false sibling_state_exists=true
```

**This is #2350’s root cause through another caller.** A fix limited to post-push cleanup would leave this path exposed.

**3. An unreadable ref is mistaken for an absent ref**

Here the session JSON stays valid. We change permissions on the existing shadow-ref file so it cannot be read.

The reproduction:

1. Creates an idle session with one pending step; listing correctly returns it.
2. Changes the shadow-ref file’s permissions to `000`.
3. Verifies that directly reading the file produces a permission error.
4. Calls session listing again.
5. Restores the ref’s permissions and runs cleanup.

What happens:

```text
Ref file exists but is unreadable
  → repository reader reports “reference not found”
  → session listing classifies the session as orphaned
  → deletes its valid state
  → restoring permissions does not restore that state
  → later cleanup deletes the unprotected branch
```

Fresh output:

```text
ref_error=reference not found list_error=<nil> state_deleted=true
```

**The important nuance:** the repository reader has already converted the permission failure into “not found.” Merely changing the caller to delete state only on `ErrReferenceNotFound` would not fix this reproduction.

**What these tests establish**

They use real disposable Git repositories and call production Go functions directly. `git fsck` confirms the synthetic shadow-only commits become unreachable. They do **not** run a complete agent session, push to a remote, or demonstrate actual transcript contents being garbage-collected.

The tests currently **assert that the buggy behavior occurs**, so `PASS` means “reproduced,” not “fixed.”
